t.en: Check whether an operation is an inner product.
Give an example of a vector space on which more than one inner product can be defined.

Use the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and the triangle inequality to reason about the size of inner products and norms of vectors.
In this section, we fix $K$ to be the field of real numbers.

A **(real) inner product space** is a real vector space $V$ equipped with an operation that assigns to any pair of vectors $\vect{u},\vect{v}\in V$ a real number $\iprod{\vect{u},\vect{v}}$, called the **inner product** of $\vect{u}$ and $\vect{v}$. This operation must satisfy the following properties:
Symmetry: $\iprod{\vect{u},\vect{v}} = \iprod{\vect{v},\vect{u}}$.
Linearity: $\iprod{\vect{u},k\vect{v}+\ell\vect{w}} = k\iprod{\vect{u},\vect{v}}+\ell\iprod{\vect{u},\vect{w}}$.
The positive definite property: $\iprod{\vect{u},\vect{u}} \geq 0$, and moreover, $\iprod{\vect{u},\vect{u}}=0$ if and only if $\vect{u} = \vect{0}$.

We now look at some properties of inner products. The first thing to note is that while the axioms require linearity in the right component, symmetry ensures that linearity in the left component also holds.
Let $V$ be an inner product space. Then $\iprod{k\vect{u}+\ell\vect{v},\vect{w}} = k\iprod{\vect{u},\vect{w}} + \ell\iprod{\vect{v},\vect{w}}$.

t.en: . In this exercise, we will work out the details of Example “Real Hilbert space”. We must show that $\Hilb_{\R}$ is a vector space. We will do this by showing that it is a subspace of $\Seq_{\R}$. Further, we must show that the inner product is well-defined. This requires some knowledge of convergent series from calculus.

Assume $a=(a_0,a_1,\ldots)$ and $b=(b_0,b_1,\ldots)$ are square summable sequences. Show that the series $a_0b_0 + a_1b_1 + a_2b_2 + \ldots$ converges to a real number. Hint: consider the series $\abs{a_0b_0} + \abs{a_1b_2} + \ldots$ and use the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and the absolute convergence test.
Using the result of part (a), show that $\Hilb_{\R}$ is a subspace of $\Seq_{\R}$.
Show that the operation $\iprod{a,b} = a_0b_0 + a_1b_1 + a_2b_2 + \ldots$ is an inner product on $\Hilb_{\R}$.
(a) By assumption, $a$ and $b$ are square summable. Let $N=a_0^2 + a_1^2 + \ldots$ and $M=b_0^2 + b_1^2 + \ldots$. By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, for all $n$, we have
Therefore the series $\abs{a_0b_0} + \abs{a_1b_1} + \ldots$ is bounded. By the absolute convergence test from calculus, it follows that the series $a_0b_0 + a_1b_1 + \ldots$ converges.

(b) It is clear that the zero sequence is square summable, and also that a scalar multiple of a square summable sequence is square summable. Hence $\Hilb_{\R}$ contains the zero vector and is closed under scalar multiplication. To show that it is closed under addition, assume $a,b\in\Hilb_{\R}$, and let $c=a+b$.
